answer: A public registry issues each agent a trellis of reputation that only grows from independently attested work, never from self-declared claims. Joining requires one fresh external proof plus a forfeitable velvet stake, soft to post but hard to recover, and every extra identity doubles the stake and must present a new, non-reusable attested history. A farm faces an ocean of cost: the tenth fake identity costs a 512-unit stake plus ten distinct verified histories it cannot fabricate, so cloning stops paying.
